title: Locally integrable conservative weak and initial forms

items.title: Locally integrable conservative weak and initial forms
items.statement:
Let $T>0$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, and let $m\ge1$ be an integer. A measurable function on an open Euclidean set $D$ is locally integrable if its norm has finite Lebesgue integral on every compact subset of $D$. For a space-time field on $\Omega\times[0,T)$ this condition is imposed on compact subsets in the relative topology, including those meeting $t=0$. Fields are identified when they agree almost everywhere. Let $U: \Omega\times[0,T)\to\mathbb R^m$, $F: \Omega\times[0,T)\to\mathbb R^{m\times3}$, and $S: \Omega\times[0,T)\to\mathbb R^m$ be such fields, and let $U_0:\Omega\to\mathbb R^m$ be locally integrable. For each row $a$, define $(\operatorname{div}_x F)_a=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}F_{aj}$ in the distributional sense, and define $F:\nabla_x\phi=\sum_{a=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^3F_{aj}\partial_{x_j}\phi_a$. The equation $\partial_tU+\operatorname{div}_xF=S$ with distributional initial datum $U_0$ means that for every $\phi\in C_c^1(\Omega\times[0,T);\mathbb R^m)$, continuously differentiable up to $t=0$ and supported away from $\partial\Omega$ and $t=T$,

$$\int_0^T\!\int_\Omega\bigl(U\cdot\partial_t\phi+F:\nabla_x\phi+S\cdot\phi\bigr)\,dx\,dt+\int_\Omega U_0(x)\cdot\phi(x,0)\,dx=0.$$

No boundary condition on $\partial\Omega$ is encoded because the test fields are supported away from it. This initial identity specifies the initial datum distributionally; it does not assert $U(\cdot,t)\to U_0$ in $L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ or any other stronger trace topology. Such a trace must be assumed or proved separately. The fields are abstract mathematical variables; no physical unit system or balance postulate is imposed.

For locally integrable scalar fields $H,R,H_0$ and a locally integrable flux $Q: \Omega\times[0,T)\to\mathbb R^3$, the inequality $\partial_tH+\operatorname{div}_x Q\ge R$ with initial datum $H_0$ means that for every nonnegative $\psi\in C_c^1(\Omega\times[0,T))$ with the same support convention,

$$\int_0^T\!\int_\Omega\bigl(H\,\partial_t\psi+Q\cdot\nabla_x\psi+R\psi\bigr)\,dx\,dt+\int_\Omega H_0(x)\psi(x,0)\,dx\le0.$$

items.title: Linear traction from shrinking local contact balance
items.statement:
Assume the axiom of countable choice: every sequence $(X_n)_{n\in\mathbb N}$ of nonempty sets has a selector $f$ with $f(n)\in X_n$. Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval containing $0$, let $B\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded open set with $C^1$ boundary, and let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open with $\overline B\subset U$. Let $\chi\in C^2(I\times U;\mathbb R^3)$ have slices $\chi_t:U\to\chi_t(U)$ that are bijections with $C^2$ inverses and $\det D_a\chi(t,a)>0$ for all $a\in U$. Write $\Omega_t=\chi_t(B)$ and $\mathcal Q=\{(s,y):s\in I,\ y\in\Omega_s\}$, and for $(t,x)\in\mathcal Q$ define $A(t,x)=\chi_t^{-1}(x)$, $u(t,x)=\partial_t\chi(t,A(t,x))$, and $D_tf=\partial_tf+(D_xf)u$; define the material acceleration $a_m:=D_tu$. At a fixed $(t,x)\in\mathcal Q$, let $\rho:\mathcal Q\to(0,\infty)$ and $b:\mathcal Q\to\mathbb R^3$ be continuously differentiable nearby. Let $\tau:\mathcal Q\times S^2\to\mathbb R^3$ be a contact traction indexed by the point $y$ and outward unit normal $n\in S^2$. In SI units, spatial and reference coordinates are measured in metres, $t$ in seconds, $\rho$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $b$ and $a_m$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, and $\tau$ in pascals, so both terms in the assumed resultant balance have units of newtons. Assume $\tau$ depends on a contact surface only through $(t,y,n)$, is continuous in $(y,n)$, and is uniformly bounded near $(t,x)$ for $n\in S^2$.

For every nonempty bounded open $C^1$ subdomain $P$ whose closure is a compact subset of $\Omega_t$, meaning that its boundary is locally a $C^1$ graph and $P$ lies locally on one side, suppose the local force balance
$$\int_{\partial P}\tau(t,y,\nu_P(y))\,dS_y+\int_P\rho(t,y)\bigl(b(t,y)-a_m(t,y)\bigr)\,dy=0$$
holds, where $\nu_P$ is the outward unit normal and $dS$ is Euclidean surface measure defined in regular charts by the Gram density $\sqrt{\det(DX^TDX)}$. Then there is a unique matrix $\sigma(t,x)\in\mathbb R^{3\times3}$ such that $\tau(t,x,n)=\sigma(t,x)n$ for every $n\in S^2$. This conclusion assumes ordinary surface traction with no surface couples or curvature-dependent singular forces.

items.title: Momentum, angular, kinetic/internal and total balance algebra
items.statement:
Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, meaning that every countable sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function. Let $I\subset\mathbb R$ be a nonempty open interval containing $0$, let $B\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty bounded open set with $C^1$ boundary, and let $U\subset\mathbb R^3$ be open with $\overline B\subset U$. Let $\chi\in C^2(I\times U;\mathbb R^3)$ have slices $\chi_t:U\to\chi_t(U)$ that are orientation-preserving bijections with $C^2$ inverses and $\det D_a\chi(t,a)>0$. Put $\Omega_t=\chi_t(B)$, $\mathcal W=\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\chi_t(U)\}$, $u(t,x)=\partial_t\chi(t,\chi_t^{-1}(x))$ on $\mathcal W$, $D_t=\partial_t+u\cdot\nabla_x$, $k=|u|^2/2$, and $E=e+k$. For each nonempty bounded $C^1$ domain $V\Subset B$ with compact closure in $B$, set $P_t=\chi_t(V)$. A bounded $C^1$ domain means a nonempty bounded open set locally on one side of a $C^1$ boundary graph; its unit normal $\nu$ points outward. All fields below are continuously differentiable on open neighborhoods of the swept closures $\{(t,x):t\in I,\ x\in\chi_t(\overline V)\}$ for each such $V$, and $\rho>0$: let $\rho$ be scalar, $u,b,q$ vector-valued, $e,r$ scalar, and $\sigma$ a $3\times3$ matrix field. Define $L=\nabla_xu$ by $L_{ij}=\partial_{x_j}u_i$, $A:B=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}B_{ij}$, $\operatorname{div}v=\sum_j\partial_{x_j}v_j$ for vector fields $v$, and $(\operatorname{div}M)_i=\sum_j\partial_{x_j}M_{ij}$ for $3\times3$ fields $M$; define $(u\otimes u)_{ij}=u_i u_j$. Interpret $\rho,u,b,\sigma,q,e,r$ as mass density, velocity, body acceleration, Cauchy stress, heat flux, specific internal energy, and specific energy supply rate. All cross products are the standard right-handed product in $\mathbb R^3$. In SI, $x,a$ are in metres, $t$ in seconds, $\rho$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $u$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $b$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$, $\sigma$ in pascals, $q$ in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, $e$ in $\mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}}$, and $r$ in $\mathrm{W\,kg^{-1}}$. The traction is $\sigma\nu$ on the outward boundary normal, and $q\cdot\nu$ is outward heat flux; thus $-\int_{\partial P_t}q\cdot\nu\,dS$ is heat entering $P_t$. Surface integrals use the chart measure with area density $\sqrt{\det(DX^TDX)}$.

Assume the continuity equation $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}(\rho u)=0$, and suppose the following integral balances hold for every such $V$ and every $t\in I$:
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{P_t}\rho u\,dx=\int_{P_t}\rho b\,dx+\int_{\partial P_t}\sigma\nu\,dS,$$
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{P_t}x\times(\rho u)\,dx=\int_{P_t}x\times(\rho b)\,dx+\int_{\partial P_t}x\times(\sigma\nu)\,dS,$$
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_{P_t}\rho E\,dx=\int_{P_t}\rho b\cdot u\,dx+\int_{\partial P_t}(\sigma\nu)\cdot u\,dS-\int_{\partial P_t}q\cdot\nu\,dS+\int_{P_t}\rho r\,dx.$$
Assume the Cauchy contact result supplies the pointwise traction $\tau=\sigma\nu$, and that its unique matrix field $\sigma$ has the stated $C^1$ regularity; the pointwise contact result alone does not imply this regularity. Then the linear momentum balance is equivalent to
$$\partial_t(\rho u)+\operatorname{div}(\rho u\otimes u-\sigma)=\rho b.$$
Together with the angular-momentum balance, it is equivalent to this momentum equation and $\sigma=\sigma^T$. The kinetic-energy identity is
$$\partial_t(\rho k)+\operatorname{div}(\rho k u-\sigma^T u)=\rho b\cdot u-\sigma:L.$$
The total-energy balance is equivalent to
$$\partial_t(\rho E)+\operatorname{div}(\rho E u-\sigma^T u+q)=\rho b\cdot u+\rho r,$$
and, after subtracting the kinetic identity, to the internal-energy equation
$$\partial_t(\rho e)+\operatorname{div}(\rho e u+q)=\sigma:L+\rho r,\qquad \rho D_t e=\sigma:L-\operatorname{div}q+\rho r.$$
Conversely, adding the kinetic and internal-energy equations recovers the total-energy equation. These are conditional identities for smooth fields; no balance postulate is derived.

items.title: Smooth weak equivalence and moving jump residual
items.statement:
Let $T>0$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be open, and let $m\ge1$ be an integer. Let $J\subset(0,T)$ and $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ be open, and let $h\in C^1(J\times D)$ have graph $\Gamma=\{(t,x',x_3):(t,x')\in J\times D,\ x_3=h(t,x')\}$ contained in an open patch $\mathcal O\subset\Omega\times(0,T)$. The minus and plus sides are $\mathcal O^-=\mathcal O\cap\{x_3<h(t,x')\}$ and $\mathcal O^+=\mathcal O\cap\{x_3>h(t,x')\}$. Let $U^\pm,S^\pm$ be $\mathbb R^m$-valued and $F^\pm$ be $\mathbb R^{m\times3}$-valued fields that are $C^1$ on their respective sides and admit $C^1$ one-sided extensions to every relatively compact part of $\Gamma$. For a matrix flux $F$, $F_j\in\mathbb R^m$ denotes its $j$th spatial column and $(\operatorname{div}_xF)_a=\sum_{j=1}^3\partial_{x_j}F_{aj}$. For any one-sided trace $G$, write $[G]=G^+-G^-$. Put $\lambda=\sqrt{1+|\nabla_{x'}h|^2}$, and define the unit normal from minus to plus and its signed normal speed by
$$n=\frac{(-\nabla_{x'}h,1)}{\lambda},\qquad V_n=\frac{\partial_t h}{\lambda}.$$
Interpret $U,F,S$ as the ordinary locally integrable piecewise functions defined by their side values and traces; no singular measure supported on $\Gamma$ is added to $S$. The interior weak identity for $\partial_tU+\operatorname{div}_xF=S$ is the test identity of the conservative weak-form definition for every $\phi\in C_c^1(\mathcal O;\mathbb R^m)$. It holds if and only if $\partial_tU^\pm+\operatorname{div}_xF^\pm=S^\pm$ on both sides and
$$[F]n-V_n[U]=0$$
on $\Gamma$. The initial-data term in the weak initial form is independent; this interior jump condition neither asserts nor requires a strong trace at $t=0$.

For scalar fields $H^\pm,R^\pm$ and vector fluxes $G^\pm$ with the same piecewise $C^1$ regularity, the interior weak inequality $\partial_tH+\operatorname{div}_xG\ge R$ means
$$\int_{\mathcal O}\bigl(H\,\partial_t\psi+G\cdot\nabla_x\psi+R\psi\bigr)\,dx\,dt\le0$$
for every nonnegative $\psi\in C_c^1(\mathcal O)$. It holds if and only if $\partial_tH^\pm+\operatorname{div}_xG^\pm\ge R^\pm$ on both sides and
$$[G]\cdot n-V_n[H]\ge0$$
on $\Gamma$. These are local equivalences for prescribed piecewise-smooth fields, not existence or uniqueness theorems for nonlinear systems. The fields are abstract mathematical variables with no assigned physical units or constitutive model.

title: Locally integrable conservative weak and initial forms — Examples

items.title: Vanishing scalar density leaves velocity undetermined by momentum
items.statement: At a fixed point, let $\rho\in[0,\infty)$ be mass density and let $u\in\mathbb R^3$ be velocity. In SI units, $\rho$ is measured in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $u$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and the momentum-density vector $M=\rho u$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$. This vector may be used as the conserved field $U$ in a conservative weak form. At $\rho=0$, distinct vectors $u_1\ne u_2$ both give $M=0$, so the momentum density does not determine velocity. At $\rho>0$, the relation has the unique inverse $u=M/\rho$. This is a pointwise algebraic example and makes no claim that any chosen fields solve a differential equation.
